# Cascading Soft-Delete, Global Read Scoping and Archive Recovery (Ash Framework v3)

## Background

`/home/user/forum` holds a Mix project (OTP app `:forum`) for a discussion-forum backend built on the
Ash Framework v3 (`ash 3.31.0`). Content is three levels deep: a post owns comments, and a comment
owns reactions.

Deleting content in this product is never destructive: removed content stays in storage, stays
invisible to ordinary readers, can be inspected by an administrator, and can be recovered later.
Recovery has to be *precise* — undoing a deletion must bring back exactly what that deletion removed
and must not resurrect content that had already been deleted by an earlier, unrelated operation.

The project currently contains only the domain shell and the project configuration. Everything
described below is missing and must be built.

## Requirements

### Domain and resources

The domain module `Forum.Content` (`lib/forum/content.ex`) must expose exactly these three
resources, each using `Ash.DataLayer.Ets` configured with `private? true`:

| Module                   | File                            | Own attribute                         |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `Forum.Content.Post`     | `lib/forum/content/post.ex`     | `title` — `:string`, public, required |
| `Forum.Content.Comment`  | `lib/forum/content/comment.ex`  | `body` — `:string`, public, required  |
| `Forum.Content.Reaction` | `lib/forum/content/reaction.ex` | `emoji` — `:string`, public, required |

Every one of the three resources also has:

* a primary key attribute named `id` of type `:uuid`, generated by default;
* a public attribute `archived_at` of type `:utc_datetime_usec`, `nil` for live records;
* a public attribute `archive_batch_id` of type `:uuid`, `nil` for live records.

Relationships:

* `Forum.Content.Post` — a to-many relationship named `:comments` pointing at
  `Forum.Content.Comment`.
* `Forum.Content.Comment` — a to-one relationship named `:post` pointing at `Forum.Content.Post`,
  backed by a required and externally writable foreign-key attribute `post_id`; and a to-many
  relationship named `:reactions` pointing at `Forum.Content.Reaction`.
* `Forum.Content.Reaction` — a to-one relationship named `:comment` pointing at
  `Forum.Content.Comment`, backed by a required and externally writable foreign-key attribute
  `comment_id`.

Aggregates:

* `Forum.Content.Post` must expose a public `count` aggregate named `comment_count` over `:comments`.
* `Forum.Content.Comment` must expose a public `count` aggregate named `reaction_count` over
  `:reactions`.

### Actions

All three resources must define these seven actions under exactly these names:

| Name             | Action type                                           | Input                                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:create`        | create                                                | the resource's own required attribute plus its foreign key (`post_id` for a comment, `comment_id` for a reaction) |
| `:read`          | read (**must be the resource's primary read action**) | none                                                                                                              |
| `:archived`      | read                                                  | none                                                                                                              |
| `:with_archived` | read                                                  | none                                                                                                              |
| `:archive`       | destroy                                               | none                                                                                                              |
| `:restore`       | update                                                | none                                                                                                              |
| `:purge`         | destroy                                               | none                                                                                                              |

"Input: none" is binding: each of those actions must succeed when invoked with an empty parameter
map and no additional arguments, e.g. `Ash.Query.for_read(Forum.Content.Post, :with_archived, %{})`,
`Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(record, :archive, %{})` and
`Ash.Changeset.for_update(record, :restore, %{})`.

### Archive semantics — action `:archive`

* Nothing is ever removed from storage by `:archive`.
* If the target record is already archived, the call still succeeds but nothing changes anywhere:
  the target keeps its existing `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id`, and no descendant is modified.
* Otherwise the target and every descendant of the target that is not already archived (a post's
  comments and those comments' reactions; a comment's reactions) are archived together as one
  generation: all of them end up with the *same* non-`nil` `archived_at` value and the *same*
  non-`nil` `archive_batch_id` value.
* Descendants that were already archived before the call keep their existing `archived_at` and
  `archive_batch_id` values byte-for-byte.
* Two separate archive operations must never produce the same `archive_batch_id`.

### Restore semantics — action `:restore`

* On a record that is not archived the call succeeds and changes nothing, anywhere.
* On an archived record: the target's `archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` both become `nil`, and
  every descendant whose `archive_batch_id` equals the target's `archive_batch_id` as it was
  immediately before the call is restored the same way (`archived_at` and `archive_batch_id` set to
  `nil`), recursively.
* Descendants carrying a different `archive_batch_id` are left exactly as they were.
* `:restore` never affects ancestors of the target.

### Purge semantics — action `:purge`

* Invoked on a record whose `archived_at` is `nil`, the action must fail and change nothing: the
  result must be `{:error, %Ash.Error.Invalid{errors: errors}}` where at least one element of
  `errors` is an `%Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges{}` whose `:fields` is `[:archived_at]` and whose
  `:message` is exactly `"must be archived before it can be purged"`.
* Invoked on an archived record, the record and every one of its descendants are permanently and
  irrecoverably removed from storage.

### Read scoping

* `:read` returns only records whose `archived_at` is `nil`. This scoping is global, not merely
  top-level: it must also hold everywhere a resource is reached indirectly — relationship loads
  (`Ash.load/3`), the `comment_count` and `reaction_count` aggregates, and filter expressions that
  traverse a relationship — so archived records can never leak into a result derived from an
  ordinary read.
* `:with_archived` returns both archived and live records.
* `:archived` returns only records whose `archived_at` is not `nil`.
* Fetching an archived record through the primary read (for example `Ash.get/3` with its default
  action) must produce an `Ash.Error.Query.NotFound`.

### Authorization

* All three resources must run `Ash.Policy.Authorizer`.
* An actor is a plain Elixir map. An actor is an administrator when its `:role` key equals `:admin`.
* With authorization enabled, the `:archived` read must be reachable only by an administrator.
  For any other actor, including `nil`, the call must return `{:error, %Ash.Error.Forbidden{}}` —
  not an empty result set.
* With authorization enabled, every other action on every resource must be permitted for every
  actor, including `nil`.

### Shared implementation modules

Three modules must be written once and shared, rather than duplicated per resource:

| Module                                    | File                                              | Behaviour                  | Must be referenced by                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Forum.Archive.Preparations.ArchiveScope` | `lib/forum/archive/preparations/archive_scope.ex` | `Ash.Resource.Preparation` | the `:read`, `:archived` and `:with_archived` actions of all three resources (directly on the action or through a resource-wide preparation) |
| `Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeArchive`    | `lib/forum/archive/changes/cascade_archive.ex`    | `Ash.Resource.Change`      | the `:archive` action of all three resources                                                                                                 |
| `Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeRestore`    | `lib/forum/archive/changes/cascade_restore.ex`    | `Ash.Resource.Change`      | the `:restore` action of all three resources                                                                                                 |

## Implementation Hints

* Project path: /home/user/forum
* The project must keep compiling as a standard Mix project: `mix compile` from
  `/home/user/forum` must succeed. Verification executes a standalone Elixir script from the
  project root with `mix run <script>` in the default `dev` Mix environment, so everything
  described above must be part of the ordinary `lib/` compilation of the `:forum` application.
* The machine has no network access. `ash 3.31.0` and `simple_sat` are already fetched and compiled
  for both the `dev` and `test` Mix environments. Do not add, remove or change dependencies in
  `mix.exs` or `mix.lock`.
* Keep `config/config.exs`'s `ash_domains: [Forum.Content]` entry intact and register all three
  resources in `Forum.Content`.
* Verification calls the actions through the plain `Ash` functions (`Ash.create/2`, `Ash.read/2`,
  `Ash.load/3`, `Ash.get/3`, `Ash.update/3`, `Ash.destroy/2`) with the action selected explicitly,
  and passes `authorize?: false` except where authorization itself is under test. Do not rely on
  domain code interfaces existing; add them only if you want them.
* Compiler warnings are tolerated; compilation errors are not.

```elixir
defmodule MyApp.Validations.IsPrime do
  # transform and validate opts

  use Ash.Resource.Validation

  @impl true
  def init(opts) do
    if opts[:field] != nil && is_atom(opts[:field]) do
      {:ok, opts}
    else
      {:error, "field must be an atom!"}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def supports(_opts), do: [Ash.Changeset]

  @impl true
  def validate(changeset, opts, _context) do
    value = Ash.Changeset.get_attribute(changeset, opts[:field])

```

### Supporting Queries in Custom Validations

To make a custom validation work on both changesets and queries, implement the `supports/1` callback:

```elixir
defmodule MyApp.Validations.ValidEmail do
  use Ash.Resource.Validation

  @impl true
  def init(opts) do
    {:ok, opts}
  end

  @impl true
  def supports(_opts), do: [Ash.Changeset, Ash.Query]

  @impl true
  def validate(subject, opts, _context) do
    value = get_value(subject, opts[:field])
    
    if is_nil(value) || valid_email?(value) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, field: opts[:field], message: "must be a valid email"}
    end
  end

  defp get_value(%Ash.Changeset{} = changeset, attribute) do
    Ash.Changeset.get_argument_or_attribute(changeset, attribute)
  end

  defp get_value(%Ash.Query{} = query, attribute) do
    Ash.Query.get_argument(query, attribute)
  end

  defp valid_email?(email) do
    String.match?(email, ~r/^[^\s]+@[^\s]+\.[^\s]+$/)
  end
end
```

This could then be used in a resource via:

```elixir
validate {MyApp.Validations.IsPrime, attribute: :foo}
```

defmodule Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges do
  @moduledoc "Used when a change is provided that covers multiple attributes/relationships"

  use Splode.Error, fields: [:fields, :message, :validation, :value], class: :invalid

  def message(error) do
    case for_fields(error) do
      "" ->
        case do_message(error) do
          "" ->
            "something went wrong"

          message ->
            message
        end

      fields ->
        case do_message(error) do
          "" ->
            "#{fields}: invalid"

          message ->
            "#{fields}: #{message}"
        end
    end
  end

  defp for_fields(%{fields: fields}) when not is_nil(fields) do
    "#{Enum.join(fields, ", ")}"
  end

  defp for_fields(_), do: ""

  defp do_message(%{message: message}) when not is_nil(message) do
    message
  end

  defp do_message(_), do: ""
end

# Changes

Changes are the primary way of customizing create/update/destroy action behavior. If you are familiar with `Plug`, you can think of an `Ash.Resource.Change` as the equivalent of a `Plug` for changesets. At its most basic, a change will take a changeset and return a new changeset. Changes can be simple, like setting or modifying an attribute value, or more complex, attaching hooks to be executed within the lifecycle of the action.

## Builtin Changes

There are a number of builtin changes that can be used, and are automatically imported into your resources. See `Ash.Resource.Change.Builtins` for more.

Some examples of usage of builtin changes

```elixir
# set the `owner` to the current actor
change relate_actor(:owner)

# set `commited_at` to the current timestamp when the action is called
change set_attribute(:committed_at, &DateTime.utc_now/0)

# optimistic lock using the `version` attribute
change optimistic_lock(:version)
```

## Custom Changes

```elixir
defmodule MyApp.Changes.Slugify do

  use Ash.Resource.Change

  # transform and validate opts
  @impl true
  def init(opts) do
    if is_atom(opts[:attribute]) do
      {:ok, opts}
    else
      {:error, "attribute must be an atom!"}
    end
  end

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, opts, _context) do
    case Ash.Changeset.fetch_change(changeset, opts[:attribute]) do
      {:ok, new_value} ->
        slug = String.replace(new_value, ~r/\s+/, "-")
        Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(changeset, opts[:attribute], slug)
      :error ->
        changeset
    end
  end
end
```

This could then be used in a resource via:

```elixir
change {MyApp.Changes.Slugify, attribute: :foo}
```

## Anonymous Function Changes

You can also use anonymous functions for changes. Keep in mind, these cannot be made atomic, or support batching. This is great for prototyping, but we generally recommend using a module, both for organizational purposes, and to allow adding atomic/batch behavior.

```elixir
change fn changeset, _context ->
  # put your code here
end
```

## Where

The `where` can be used to perform changes conditionally. This functions by running the validations in the `where`, and if the validation returns an error, we discard the error and skip the operation. This means that even custom validations can be used in conditions.

For example:

```elixir
change {Slugify, attribute: :foo} do
  where [attribute_equals(:slugify, true)]
end
```

## Action vs Global Changes

You can place a change on any create, update, or destroy action. For example:

```elixir
actions do
  create :create do
    change {Slugify, attribute: :name}
  end
end
```

Or you can use the global changes block to apply to all actions of a given type. Where statements can be used in both cases. Use `on` to determine the types of actions the validation runs on. By default, it only runs on create and update actions.

```elixir
changes do
  change {Slugify, attribute: :name} do
    on [:create]
  end
end
```

The changes section allows you to add changes across multiple actions of a resource.

defmodule Ash.Resource.Change.CascadeDestroy do
  @option_schema [
    relationship: [
      type: :atom,
      doc: "The name of the relationship to work on",
      required: true
    ],
    action: [
      type: :atom,
      doc:
        "The name of the destroy action to call on the related resource. Uses the primary destroy by default.",
      required: false
    ],
    read_action: [
      type: :atom,
      doc:
        "The name of the read action to call on the related resource to find results to be destroyed",
      required: false
    ],
    return_notifications?: [
      type: :boolean,
      doc: "Return notifications for all destroyed records?",
      required: false,
      default: false
    ],
    after_action?: [
      type: :boolean,
      doc:
        "If true, cascade destroys are done in after_action hooks. If false, they run as before_action hooks. Defaults to true for atomic action compatibility",
      required: false,
      default: true
    ],
    domain: [
      type: {:spark, Ash.Domain},
      private?: true
    ]
  ]

  option_schema = @option_schema

  defmodule Opts do
    @moduledoc false
    use Spark.Options.Validator, schema: option_schema
  end

  @moduledoc """
  Cascade a resource's destroy action to a related resource's destroy action.

  ## Timing Control

  The `after_action?` option controls when the cascade destroy occurs:

  - `after_action?: true` (default) - Runs as an after-action hook, making it safe for atomic actions
  - `after_action?: false` - Runs as a before-action hook

  When `after_action?: true`, the change adds an after-action hook that explicitly
  calls destroy on any records related via the named relationship. It will optimise
  for bulk destroys where possible. This makes it safe to use in atomic actions, but
  might not be possible depending on the data layer setup (see warning below).

  When `after_action?: false`, the change simply runs as a before_action.
  Requires keyset pagination on the primary read action of the targeted relation.

  > #### Beware database constraints {: .warning}
  >
  > Think carefully before using this change with data layers which enforce
  > referential integrity (ie PostgreSQL and SQLite) and you may need to defer
  > constraints for the relationship in question.
  >
  > See also:
  >   1. [`postgres.references.reference.deferrable` DSL](https://hexdocs.pm/ash_postgres/dsl-ashpostgres-datalayer.html#postgres-references-reference-deferrable)
  >   2. [`sqlite.references.reference.deferrable` DSL](https://hexdocs.pm/ash_sqlite/dsl-ashsqlite-datalayer.html#sqlite-references-reference-deferrable)
  >   3. [PostgreSQL's `SET CONSTRAINTS` documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-set-constraints.html)
  >   4. [SQLite's `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys` documentation](https://www.sqlite.org/pragma.html#pragma_defer_foreign_keys)

  > #### Cascading notifications {: .tip}
  >
  > By default notifications are disabled for the related destroy. This is to avoid potentially sending a **lot** of notifications for high-cardinality relationships.

  ## Options

  #{Opts.docs()}

  ## Example

      change {Ash.Resource.Change.CascadeDestroy, relationship: :comments, action: :destroy}

    or, equivalently using `Ash.Resource.Change.Builtins.cascade_destroy/2`:

      change cascade_destroy(:comments, action: :destroy)

  """
  use Ash.Resource.Change
  import Ash.Gettext
  require Ash.Query

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def change(changeset, opts, context) do
    with {:ok, %Opts{} = opts} <- Opts.validate(opts),
         {:ok, opts} <- validate_relationship_and_action(opts, changeset.resource) do
      if not opts.after_action? and
           opts.relationship.type in [:many_to_many, :has_many, :has_one] do
        Ash.Changeset.before_action(changeset, fn changeset ->
          # can't produce `{:error, error}` because `changeset.phase` is before_action
          case {destroy_related([changeset.data], opts, context, changeset),
                opts.return_notifications?} do
            {_, false} ->
              changeset

            {%{notifications: []}, true} ->
              changeset

            {%{notifications: notifications}, true} ->
              {changeset, %{notifications: notifications}}
          end
        end)
      else
        Ash.Changeset.after_action(changeset, fn changeset, result ->
          case {destroy_related([result], opts, context, changeset), opts.return_notifications?} do
            {{:error, error}, _} ->
              {:error, error}

            {_, false} ->
              {:ok, result}

            {%{notifications: []}, true} ->
              {:ok, result}

            {%{notifications: notifications}, true} ->
              {:ok, result, notifications}
          end
        end)
      end
    else
      {:error, reason} ->
        Ash.Changeset.add_error(changeset, reason)
    end
  end

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def atomic(%{resource: resource}, opts, _) do
    with {:ok, %Opts{} = opts} <- Opts.validate(opts),
         {:ok, opts} <- validate_relationship_and_action(opts, resource) do
      if not opts.after_action? and
           opts.relationship.type in [:many_to_many, :has_many, :has_one] do
        {:not_atomic, "Need to destroy relationships in a before batch"}
      else
        :ok
      end
    else
      {:error, error} ->
        {:error, error}
    end
  end

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def before_batch([%{resource: resource} = changeset | _] = changesets, opts, context) do
    with {:ok, %Opts{} = opts} <- Opts.validate(opts),
         {:ok, opts} <- validate_relationship_and_action(opts, resource) do
      records = Enum.map(changesets, & &1.data)

      if not opts.after_action? and
           opts.relationship.type in [:many_to_many, :has_many, :has_one] do
        case {destroy_related(records, opts, context, changeset), opts.return_notifications?} do
          {{:error, error}, _} ->
            Enum.map(changesets, &Ash.Changeset.add_error(&1, error))

          {_, false} ->
            changesets

          {%{notifications: empty}, true} when empty in [nil, []] ->
            changesets

          {%{notifications: notifications}, true} ->
            Enum.concat(changesets, notifications)

          {:ok, _} ->
            changesets
        end
      else
        changesets
      end
    else
      {:error, reason} -> [{:error, reason}]
    end
  end

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def after_batch(
        [{%{resource: resource} = changeset, _} | _] = changesets_and_results,
        opts,
        context
      ) do
    with {:ok, %Opts{} = opts} <- Opts.validate(opts),
         {:ok, opts} <- validate_relationship_and_action(opts, resource) do
      records = Enum.map(changesets_and_results, &elem(&1, 1))
      result = Enum.map(records, &{:ok, &1})

      if not opts.after_action? and
           opts.relationship.type in [:many_to_many, :has_many, :has_one] do
        result
      else
        case {destroy_related(records, opts, context, changeset), opts.return_notifications?} do
          {{:error, error}, _} ->
            Enum.map(result, fn _ -> {:error, error} end)

          {_, false} ->
            result

          {%{notifications: empty}, true} when empty in [nil, []] ->
            result

          {%{notifications: notifications}, true} ->
            Enum.concat(result, notifications)
        end
      end
    else
      {:error, reason} -> [{:error, reason}]
    end
  end

  # @impl true
  # def batch_change(changesets, _opts, _context) do
  #   changesets
  # end

  @doc false
  @impl true
  def batch_callbacks?([], _, _), do: false
  def batch_callbacks?(_, _, _), do: true

  @doc false
  def opt_schema, do: @option_schema

  defp validate_relationship_and_action(opts, resource) do
    case Ash.Resource.Info.relationship(resource, opts.relationship) do
      nil ->
        {:error,
         Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidRelationship.exception(
           relationship: opts.relationship,
           message: error_message("Relationship doesn't exist.")
         )}

      relationship ->
        if opts.action do
          case Ash.Resource.Info.action(relationship.destination, opts.action) do
            action when action.type == :destroy ->
              {:ok,
               %{
                 opts
                 | action: action,
                   relationship: relationship,
                   domain:
                     relationship.domain || Ash.Resource.Info.domain(relationship.destination)
               }}

            _ ->
              {:error,
               Ash.Error.Invalid.NoSuchAction.exception(
                 resource: relationship.destination,
                 action: opts.action,
                 destroy: :destroy
               )}
          end
        else
          {:ok,
           %{
             opts
             | action: Ash.Resource.Info.primary_action!(relationship.destination, :destroy),
               relationship: relationship,
               domain: relationship.domain || Ash.Resource.Info.domain(relationship.destination)
           }}
        end
    end
  end

  defp destroy_related([], _, _, _), do: :ok

  defp destroy_related(data, opts, context, changeset) do
    action = opts.action
    relationship = opts.relationship

    context_opts =
      context
      |> Ash.Context.to_opts(
        domain: opts.domain,
        return_errors?: true,
        strategy: [:stream, :atomic, :atomic_batches],
        return_notifications?: opts.return_notifications?
      )

    action_context =
      Map.merge(relationship.context || %{}, %{
        cascade_destroy: true,
        accessing_from: %{source: relationship.source, name: relationship.name}
      })

    context_opts =
      Keyword.update(
        context_opts,
        :context,
        action_context,
        &Map.merge(&1, action_context)
      )

    case related_query(data, opts, context_opts) do
      {:ok, query} ->
        Ash.bulk_destroy!(
          query,
          action.name,
          %{},
          context_opts
        )

      :error ->
        if changeset.phase == :after_action and changeset.action_type == :destroy do
          {:error,
           "Unable to cascade destroy for #{relationship.name} relationship in after_action"}
        else
          read_action_name =
            opts.read_action || opts.relationship.read_action || opts.action.atomic_upgrade_with

          load_query =
            if read_action_name do
              opts.relationship.destination
              |> Ash.Query.for_read(
                read_action_name,
                relationship_read_action_arguments(opts.relationship),
                scope: context
              )
              |> Ash.Query.set_context(%{
                cascade_destroy: true,
                accessing_from: %{source: relationship.source, name: relationship.name}
              })
            else
              Ash.Query.set_context(relationship.destination, %{
                cascade_destroy: true,
                accessing_from: %{source: relationship.source, name: relationship.name}
              })
            end

          data
          |> List.wrap()
          |> Ash.load!(
            [{relationship.name, load_query}],
            scope: context
          )
          |> Enum.flat_map(fn record ->
            record
            |> Map.get(relationship.name)
            |> List.wrap()
          end)
          |> Ash.bulk_destroy!(
            action.name,
            %{},
            Keyword.update(
              context_opts,
              :context,
              action_context,
              &Map.merge(&1, action_context)
            )
          )
        end
    end
  end

  defp related_query(_records, opts, _) when opts.relationship.type == :many_to_many, do: :error

  defp related_query(records, opts, context_opts) do
    read_action_name =
      opts.read_action || opts.relationship.read_action || opts.action.atomic_upgrade_with

    read_action =
      if read_action_name do
        Ash.Resource.Info.action(opts.relationship.destination, read_action_name)
      else
        Ash.Resource.Info.primary_action!(opts.relationship.destination, :read)
      end

    related_query =
      Ash.Query.for_read(
        opts.relationship.destination,
        read_action.name,
        relationship_read_action_arguments(opts.relationship),
        context_opts
      )

    related_query =
      Ash.Actions.Read.Relationships.related_query(
        opts.relationship.name,
        records,
        related_query,
        Ash.Query.new(opts.relationship.source)
      )
      |> elem(1)
      |> filter_by_keys(opts.relationship, records)

    if Ash.Actions.Read.Relationships.has_parent_expr?(
         opts.relationship,
         related_query.context,
         related_query.domain
       ) do
      :error
    else
      {:ok, related_query}
    end
  end

  defp filter_by_keys(query, %{no_attributes?: true}, _records) do
    query
  end

  defp filter_by_keys(
         query,
         %{source_attribute: source_attribute, destination_attribute: destination_attribute},
         records
       ) do
    source_values = Enum.map(records, &Map.get(&1, source_attribute))

    Ash.Query.filter(query, ^ref(destination_attribute) in ^source_values)
  end

  defp relationship_read_action_arguments(relationship) do
    Map.get(relationship, :read_action_arguments, %{})
  end
end

defmodule Forum.Archive.Changes.CascadeArchive do
  use Ash.Resource.Change
  require Ash.Query

  @impl true
  def change(changeset, _opts, _context) do
    if not is_nil(changeset.data.archived_at) do
      # Target is already archived, do nothing.
      changeset
    else
      archived_at = Ash.Changeset.get_argument(changeset, :archived_at) || DateTime.utc_now()
      archive_batch_id = Ash.Changeset.get_argument(changeset, :archive_batch_id) || Ash.UUID.generate()

      changeset =
        changeset
        |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archived_at, archived_at)
        |> Ash.Changeset.force_change_attribute(:archive_batch_id, archive_batch_id)

      Ash.Changeset.before_action(changeset, fn changeset ->
        cascade_archive(changeset.data, archived_at, archive_batch_id)
        changeset
      end)
    end
  end

  defp cascade_archive(%Forum.Content.Post{} = post, archived_at, archive_batch_id) do
    comments =
      Forum.Content.Comment
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived)
      |> Ash.Query.filter(post_id == ^post.id)
      |> Ash.read!()

    for comment <- comments do
      if is_nil(comment.archived_at) do
        comment
        |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{archived_at: archived_at, archive_batch_id: archive_batch_id})
        |> Ash.destroy!()
      else
        cascade_archive(comment, archived_at, archive_batch_id)
      end
    end
  end

  defp cascade_archive(%Forum.Content.Comment{} = comment, archived_at, archive_batch_id) do
    reactions =
      Forum.Content.Reaction
      |> Ash.Query.for_read(:with_archived)
      |> Ash.Query.filter(comment_id == ^comment.id)
      |> Ash.read!()

    for reaction <- reactions do
      if is_nil(reaction.archived_at) do
        reaction
        |> Ash.Changeset.for_destroy(:archive, %{archived_at: archived_at, archive_batch_id: archive_batch_id})
        |> Ash.destroy!()
      end
    end
  end

  defp cascade_archive(%Forum.Content.Reaction{}, _archived_at, _archive_batch_id) do
    :ok
  end
end

defmodule TestArchiving do
  def run do
    IO.puts "=== Starting Archiving Tests ==="

    # 1. Create a Post, some Comments, and some Reactions
    post1 = Ash.create!(Post, :create, %{title: "Post 1"})
    comment1 = Ash.create!(Comment, :create, %{body: "Comment 1", post_id: post1.id})

    reaction2 = Ash.create!(Reaction, :create, %{emoji: "❤️", comment_id: comment1.id})
    reaction3 = Ash.create!(Reaction, :create, %{emoji: "😮", comment_id: comment2.id})

    # Verify initial state
    assert is_nil(post1.archived_at)
    assert is_nil(comment1.archived_at)
    assert is_nil(reaction1.archived_at)

    # Verify count aggregates
    post_loaded = Ash.load!(post1, [:comment_count, :comments])
    assert post_loaded.comment_count == 2
    assert length(post_loaded.comments) == 2

    comment_loaded = Ash.load!(comment1, [:reaction_count, :reactions])
    assert comment_loaded.reaction_count == 2
    assert length(comment_loaded.reactions) == 2

    IO.puts "Initial state verified successfully."

    # 2. Test archiving a single Comment first (to test byte-for-byte preservation of already archived descendants)
    # Let's archive comment2 first
    comment2_archived = Ash.destroy!(comment2, action: :archive)
    assert not is_nil(comment2_archived.archived_at)
    assert not is_nil(comment2_archived.archive_batch_id)

    # Let's archive reaction3 as well
    reaction3_archived = Ash.destroy!(reaction3, action: :archive)

    # Wait, let's load post1 again and check aggregates
    post_loaded2 = Ash.load!(post1, [:comment_count, :comments])
    # comment2 is archived, so it should NOT be in comments or comment_count
    assert post_loaded2.comment_count == 1
    assert Enum.map(post_loaded2.comments, & &1.id) == [comment1.id]

    # 3. Test archiving Post 1 (this cascades to comment1, reaction1, reaction2, but comment2 and reaction3 should keep their original batch IDs)
    post1_archived = Ash.destroy!(post1, action: :archive)
    assert not is_nil(post1_archived.archived_at)
    assert not is_nil(post1_archived.archive_batch_id)

    # Read comment1, reaction1, reaction2, comment2, reaction3 with_archived
    comment1_loaded = Ash.get!(Comment, comment1.id, action: :with_archived)
    comment2_loaded = Ash.get!(Comment, comment2.id, action: :with_archived)
    reaction1_loaded = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction1.id, action: :with_archived)
    reaction2_loaded = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction2.id, action: :with_archived)
    reaction3_loaded = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction3.id, action: :with_archived)

    # Check comment1 generation matches post1
    assert comment1_loaded.archived_at == post1_archived.archived_at
    assert comment1_loaded.archive_batch_id == post1_archived.archive_batch_id

    # Check reactions match post1
    assert reaction1_loaded.archived_at == post1_archived.archived_at
    assert reaction1_loaded.archive_batch_id == post1_archived.archive_batch_id
    assert reaction2_loaded.archived_at == post1_archived.archived_at
    assert reaction2_loaded.archive_batch_id == post1_archived.archive_batch_id

    # Check comment2 and reaction3 keep their original values
    assert comment2_loaded.archive_batch_id == comment2_archived.archive_batch_id
    assert comment2_loaded.archive_batch_id != post1_archived.archive_batch_id
    assert reaction3_loaded.archive_batch_id == reaction3_archived.archive_batch_id

    IO.puts "Archive semantics and cascade verified successfully."

    # 4. Test Ash.get and read scoping on archived records
    case Ash.get(Post, post1.id) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}} ->
        IO.puts "Ash.get/3 correctly returns NotFound for archived record."
      other ->
        raise "Expected Ash.get to return NotFound for archived record, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    post1_restored = Ash.update!(post1_archived, :restore)
    assert is_nil(post1_restored.archived_at)
    assert is_nil(post1_restored.archive_batch_id)

    comment1_restored = Ash.get!(Comment, comment1.id, action: :with_archived)
    comment2_restored = Ash.get!(Comment, comment2.id, action: :with_archived)
    reaction1_restored = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction1.id, action: :with_archived)
    reaction2_restored = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction2.id, action: :with_archived)
    reaction3_restored = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction3.id, action: :with_archived)

    assert is_nil(comment1_restored.archived_at)
    assert is_nil(reaction1_restored.archived_at)
    assert is_nil(reaction2_restored.archived_at)

    # comment2 and reaction3 must remain archived
    assert not is_nil(comment2_restored.archived_at)
    assert not is_nil(reaction3_restored.archived_at)

    IO.puts "Restore semantics and precise recovery verified successfully."

    # 6. Test Purge Semantics
    # Calling purge on a live record must fail
    case Ash.destroy(post1_restored, action: :purge) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Invalid{errors: errors}} ->
        invalid_change = Enum.find(errors, fn
          %Ash.Error.Changes.InvalidChanges{fields: [:archived_at], message: "must be archived before it can be purged"} -> true
          _ -> false
        end)
        if invalid_change do
          IO.puts "Purging active record failed with correct error as expected."
        else
          raise "Expected InvalidChanges on :archived_at, got: #{inspect(errors)}"
        end
      other ->
        raise "Expected error when purging active record, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    # Now let's archive comment1 (which archives comment1, reaction1, reaction2)
    comment1_archived = Ash.destroy!(comment1_restored, action: :archive)
    assert not is_nil(comment1_archived.archived_at)

    # Now let's purge comment1. This should permanently delete comment1, reaction1, reaction2 from storage!
    Ash.destroy!(comment1_archived, action: :purge)

    # Verify they are gone from storage (even with_archived read)
    case Ash.get(Comment, comment1.id, action: :with_archived) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}} ->
        IO.puts "Comment 1 successfully purged."
      other ->
        raise "Expected comment1 to be gone, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    case Ash.get(Reaction, reaction1.id, action: :with_archived) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}} ->
        IO.puts "Reaction 1 successfully purged."
      other ->
        raise "Expected reaction1 to be gone, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    case Ash.get(Reaction, reaction2.id, action: :with_archived) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Query.NotFound{}} ->
        IO.puts "Reaction 2 successfully purged."
      other ->
        raise "Expected reaction2 to be gone, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    # Verify comment2 and reaction3 are STILL in storage
    _ = Ash.get!(Comment, comment2.id, action: :with_archived)
    _ = Ash.get!(Reaction, reaction3.id, action: :with_archived)
    IO.puts "Purge semantics and cascading purge verified successfully."

    # 7. Test Authorization
    # :archived read action must be reachable only by an administrator
    case Ash.read(Post, action: :archived, actor: %{role: :admin}, authorize?: true) do
      {:ok, _} ->
        IO.puts "Admin actor can access :archived action."
      other ->
        raise "Expected admin to be able to access :archived, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    case Ash.read(Post, action: :archived, actor: %{role: :user}, authorize?: true) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Forbidden{}} ->
        IO.puts "Non-admin actor is forbidden from accessing :archived."
      other ->
        raise "Expected non-admin actor to be forbidden, got: #{inspect(other)}"
    end

    case Ash.read(Post, action: :archived, actor: nil, authorize?: true) do
      {:error, %Ash.Error.Forbidden{}} ->
        IO.puts "Nil actor is forbidden from accessing :archived."
      other ->

    # Other actions must be permitted for every actor, including nil
    _post2 = Ash.create!(Post, :create, %{title: "Post 2"}, actor: nil, authorize?: true)
    IO.puts "Other actions are permitted for everyone."

    IO.puts "=== All tests passed successfully! ==="
  end

  defp assert(true), do: :ok
  defp assert(false), do: raise "Assertion failed!"
end
